chunks: And by his chain, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Fadhl, who said:

I saw Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) when he intended to bid farewell before departing for 'Umrah. He approached the grave from the side of the head of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) after sunset, then offered salām to the Prophet (peace be upon him) and clung to the grave. Then he went to the pulpit, then turned back until he reached the grave, stood beside it, and prayed, pressing his left shoulder against the grave, close to the pillar that is below the carved, ringed pillar at the head of the Prophet (peace be upon him). He prayed six or eight rak'ahs while wearing his sandals. He said: The duration of his ruku' and sujud was three tasbihāt or more. When he finished that, he prostrated for a long prostration until his sweat moistened the pebbles. He said: And some of our companions mentioned that they saw him pressing his cheek to the ground of the mosque.
ai.seo_question: What were the specific rituals and actions performed by Imam al-Rida when bidding farewell to the Prophet Muhammad before 'Umrah?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the Imam’s deep reverence for the Prophet’s resting place, specifically noting his prayer near the 'Ustuwana al-Khalaqa' (the carved pillar) at the head of the grave, a detail significant in Shia jurisprudence regarding the location of the Prophet's burial. The prolonged prostration, marked by sweat moistening the stones, underscores the spiritual intensity of bidding farewell (Tawarrud) to the Messenger of Allah before embarking on a pilgrimage.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 3. All of my scholars narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali ibn Faďďāl, who said:

I saw Abal Ḥasan (Imam Riďā (a.s.)) bidding farewell (to the Messenger of Allāh (s.a.a.w.)) when he wanted to go for ‘Umrah. It was after sunset when he approached the grave of the Messenger of Allāh (s.a.a.w.) from the direction of the head. He said Salām to the Messenger of Allāh (s.a.a.w.) and clung to the grave. Then he came to the pulpit of the Messenger of Allāh (s.a.a.w.). Thereafter, he moved back to the grave and established prayers (so close to the grave that) his left shoulder touched the part of the grave which is close to a pillar. This pillar is situated on the opposite side of (another) pillar which is by the head of the Prophet (s.a.a.w.). He prayed six or eight Rak’ah while wearing his sandals and the length of his RUKŪ’ and SUJŪD was as long as reciting TASBǏḤĀT three or more times. After he finished his prayers, he prostrated for such a long time that the sand (on which he had prostrated) became moistened from his sweat. And some of our companions added that he was seen placing his cheek on the ground of the Mosque.
